kata.name: Flyweight near-floor control: one client, one key, one flyweight — the rerouted handle is caught by the frozen conventional contract and by equation eq0; the control self-negates
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md (Flyweight row, re-opened by naming the law first); fixtures/katas/flyweight/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.8
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: at the one-client floor the frozen conventional contract (handle identity + interning pairs + pool closure) catches every injected fault; the probe's eq0 violation maps to the same handle element, so unique is empty and the control must be killed

expected.detail: client 0 holds Flyweight row 1 while factory(key(client 0)) is row 0; equation 0 (lhs key x factory, rhs flyweight) fires on row 0 with lhs row 0 and rhs row 1. The conventional arm names the same handle element plus the orphaned pool row 1

commands: python3 prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 2 clean + 4 fault fixtures match the pre-registered detections
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/flyweight/control-floor-fault-rerouted-handle.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert, executed before the probe arm: the complete conventional Flyweight contract identifies the handle element of the single client and the orphaned pool row, so it catches everything the probe can see at the floor

baseline.artifact: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py sha256:c5c9c28bc4e1bb75a7b2fb64bf41a66d908cd3fee468f7fd00150c26cdbd6d30 (scripted conventional Flyweight test: handle identity, interning pairs, pool closure)

expressibility_gap.invariant: control scope: every injected fault lies inside the single declared client/key/flyweight instance the frozen contract covers
expressibility_gap.why: the near-floor control measures what a complete conventional Flyweight test catches at the smallest instance; it says nothing about faults outside the declared instance, which is the positives' scoped claim

discrepancies: the control fault trips two conventional assertions (handle identity and pool closure) while the probe sees only the handle violation; the asymmetry is baseline-only and cannot create a unique detection, since unique = probe elements - baseline elements
procedure: 1. The law was named before the fixtures (README 'Law named first'): F-Intern (declarative key on the intrinsic tuple), F-Handle (path equation key x factory = flyweight), plus the two laws named as unexpressible (F-Closure, F-Capacity). The fault set and its expectations were pinned in fixtures/katas/flyweight/faults.json.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/flyweight_baseline.py, sha256 pinned in comparison.baseline) was executed first: the complete conventional Flyweight contract (handle identity per client, interning pairs over declared rows, pool closure), never calling catherine.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, findings recorded verbatim; no kernel change and no new CLI.

4. Witnesses were mapped to the pre-registered element vocabulary: an equation witness {equation, row} to flyweight:handle-identity@Client#<row>; a key witness {key, rows:[lo,hi]} to flyweight:interning-pair@Flyweight#<lo>/Flyweight#<hi>; baseline-only pool-closure elements carry no probe counterpart. unique = probe elements minus baseline elements.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived. Expressibility is recorded separately in expressibility_gap and never inflates the verdict.
